Phys. 69, 3885 (1978)) and Wiese et al. 1989 could not be opened; only Klose 1967 (2p1-2p4, abstract) is stored and 30.2 ns for 2p9 stays the Vassen-review value.

Lifetimes of the resonance levels 4s[3/2]1 and 4s'[1/2]1 and of the 5s, 3d, 4d, 5p levels drawn: none located in an open source (Inoue, Setser, Sadeghi 1982 abstract: Ar(5p) lifetimes 100-140 ns, 5s and 3d about 50 ns, no level-resolved numbers).
Welte et al. 2009 and Klein et al. 1996 primary papers not opened; their numbers are second-hand from Williams et al. (arXiv:1012.4509 turned out to be Williams et al., not Welte).
Absolute (frequency-comb) frequencies of the 4s-4p lines: none located.
conflicts: 39Ar hyperfine A constants: Williams et al. 2011 [A(4s[3/2]2) = -285.36(13), A(4p[5/2]3) = -134.36(8) MHz] vs Welte et al. 2009 [-287.15(14), -135.16(12) MHz]: 1-2 MHz apart with ~0.1 MHz claimed uncertainties; the ratio A(4s)/A(4p) agrees to <0.1%. B constants agree. Williams (checked on 83Kr) is used.
g_J(4s[3/2]2): atomic-beam value 1.500964(8) (Lurio et al. 1960) vs 1.506 in NIST ASD (older optical value).

Keto & Kuo 1981 also assign 61 +- 10 ns to 3d'[3/2]1 (115366.866 cm^-1) and 61 +- 6 ns to 3d[3/2]1 (114147.732 cm^-1). Both are J = 1 resonance levels whose NIST A values to the ground state are 3.13e8 and 2.70e8 s^-1 (natural lifetime of a few ns), so the 61 ns figures are radiation-trapped cascade lifetimes at 2-3000 Torr and were NOT stored as level lifetimes.
Klose 1967 lifetimes of 2p1-2p4 carry 5-15 % systematic errors by the author's own estimate; treat as low-accuracy values.
notes: Isotope-shift keys 'A-B' mean nu(A) - nu(B); heavier argon isotopes lie at higher frequency on 811.5 nm (Table III of Williams et al. is given relative to 38Ar: Delta nu(38,A') = nu(A') - nu(38)), while the 800.8 and 922.7 nm shifts of Chu et al. are printed relative to 40Ar. 39Ar and 37Ar are radioactive (ATTA tracers). Level energies are NIST ASD values from data/ar/levels.csv; Paschen names in the labels. Entries marked '(abstract)' were read on the publisher's abstract page only. Added 2026-10-01 (second pass): the 105 nm measurements of Velchev et al. are from 1999 (older than 20 years), so the NIST energy stays in use; isotope shifts of that line are printed as nu(40) - nu(A). Paschen-labelled lifetimes (Klose) were assigned to NIST levels by energy order.
